content.title: Where to watch Spurs vs. Trail Blazers NBA game tonight on free streams, TV
content.text: San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper, left, and Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham, right, scramble for a loose ball during the second half of an NBA basketball game in San Antonio, Thursday, March 5, 2026. (AP Photo/Eric Gay)APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Dustin Hockensmith | dhockensmith@pennlive.comTwo nights after clinching their first 60-win season in a decade, the San Antonio Spurs are back at the Frost Bank Center Wednesday night for a matchup with the Portland Trail Blazers. The game is scheduled to start at 9:30 p.m. ET (8:30 p.m. CT) with TV coverage on ESPN and streaming on-demand.How to watch Spurs vs. Trail Blazers on TV and stream without cable:When: Wednesday, April 8 at 9:30 p.m. ET (8:30 p.m. CT)Where: Frost Bank Center, San Antonio, TexasTV channel: ESPNStreaming on: FuboTV (free trial) | DirecTV (free trial) | SlingTV (low intro rate) | ESPN Unlimited ($29.99/mo.)The pennlive.com logoA subscription is required to read this story.Subscribe now to continue.Spurs vs. Trail Blazers: The matchupNotable for this matchup is the anticipated absence of young Spurs star Victor Wembanyama, who is listed as doubtful with a rib contusion he suffered in the first half of Monday’s 115-102 win over the Philadelphia 76ers. San Antonio is still listed as a 2.5-point betting favorite on its home floor even without its MVP candidate after Stephon Castle led a group of six double-digit scorers to victory over the 76ers with 19 points, 10 rebounds and 13 assists in 31 minutes. The Spurs enter Wednesday’s matchup with a 60-19 record and sit in second place in the Western Conference behind the Oklahoma City Thunder, who improved to 63-16 on Tuesday night. The Trail Blazers are locked into the West’s Play-In Tournament with their 40-39 record, which is good for ninth place currently with a shot to move as high as the No. 8 seed. Portland comes off a Monday night overtime loss in Denver to Nikola Jokic and the Nuggets (137-132) that snapped a three-game winning streak. The Trail Blazers are in the midst of a strong finish to the regular season with an 8-3 mark over 11 games prior to their road finale in San Antonio. Day passes are also available for 24 hours ($4.99), as well as three-day ($9.99) and seven-day access ($14.99).ESPN Unlimited ($29.99 bundle): ESPN has a new, standalone package that includes ABC broadcasts, all of ESPN’s sports channels, and access to ESPN+.
